chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said:
When the woman who has not been consummated is divorced, she becomes irrevocably divorced with one divorce.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce before consummation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that for a wife who has not yet been consummated, a single pronouncement of divorce results in an irrevocable separation (banan), a ruling distinct from the standard three-divorce process required for consummated marriages. This establishes the principle that the 'waiting period' (iddah) for such women is shorter and the marital bond is severed immediately upon the first talaq, reflecting the specific legal status of the marriage contract prior to intimacy. The narration underscores the precision of Shia jurisprudence in distinguishing between partial and full marital rights based on consummation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘When the woman is divorced, the one whose marriage has not been consummated, she is irrevocably divorced with the one divorce’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a woman with whom her husband has not gone to bed is divorced, she becomes stranger to him by one divorce/”
